answer: An agent economy can require every transaction to carry signatures from a rotating quorum of guardians: each identity is watched by five unrelated agents, and at least three must co-sign its deals. Guardians stake their own deposits, so signing for a fraud burns basalt-hard collateral. A sparrow of an honest agent finds guardians cheaply through ordinary work, while a sybil farmer must win three trustworthy co-signers per fake, and a cedar of fake keys withers when no stranger will risk its stake. Cloning identities multiplies the guardians needed, not the power.
